label: Drawer
title: Drawer
summary: Use a Drawer for a panel that peeks from the bottom of a screen and drags up to show more, such as recent transactions.
corePrinciple: Always there: a peek, or pulled up to read more.

anatomy.title: A handle, a title, and scrolling content
anatomy.description: The grey sheet carries a drag handle and an optional title that stay put while the content scrolls. Collapsed, only its top peeks above the screen’s bottom edge.
blocks: A button: press it, or drag it or the content, to resize.

configuration.title: Peek, title, and scrim
configuration.description: Set how much of the drawer peeks when collapsed, so the title and the first item show. A scrim dims the screen while the drawer covers it.

states.title: Collapsed or expanded
states.description: A Drawer has two sizes and springs between them when dragged or when its handle is pressed; Escape collapses it. It never closes: collapsed is its smallest size.
blocks: The peek shows what’s inside and invites a drag.
The sheet rises to near the top; the list scrolls inside it.

sizing.title: Full width, sized by the screen
sizing.description: The drawer spans the screen it sits in. Collapsed, it shows 200 px by default; expanded, it is 90% of that screen’s height, and never more than 95%. Its content starts 71 px below the top of the sheet, as in Figma.

content.title: Name it, and lead with what matters
content.description: Title the drawer with what it holds. Collapsed, people see only the title and the first item or two, so put the most useful item first.

inContext.title: Recent transactions on a home screen
inContext.description: The drawer peeks under the home screen. People drag it or press its handle to expand it, and the screen’s See all transactions button opens it too.

sources.title: Use the public Drawer contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (23 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Drawer is one 360 × 722 component with a fixed header and a scrolling content slot. The package sizes the drawer from the screen it sits in, and its content starts 71 px from the top, as in Figma. It can be dragged with a mouse or a finger; its handle is a button that expands or collapses it, and Escape collapses it. On the web it’s a dialog named by its title. It has no way to close, and its scrim leaves keyboard focus alone. On this site drags spring slightly differently from Storybook because the site uses a simplified animation library.
